newsitem.title: USA: NYS Democrats blast gov over welfare surplus - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS Democrats blast gov over welfare surplus - paper.

text.p: New York State Democrats attacked Gov George Pataki for planning to use a welfare surplus for tax cuts instead of programs that would move more people off the rolls, the New York Post said on Monday.

In a letter sent to Pataki on Monday, 17 Democrat House members criticized Pataki for diverting $416 million from welfare programs. As the state's welfare caseloads have gone down over the past two years, the state will get an extra $730 million this year and next, under new federal welfare laws.

A draft of Pataki's budget showed he plans to use $416 million of that windfall to "provide needed fiscal relief to state and local taxpayers," the paper said. The rest would go to a variety of programs, including job training.

Nita Lowey, D-Queens, one of the letter's writers, told the Post that using the funds for tax cuts violated the "spirit of the welfare reform laws." But a spokesman for the governor was quoted by the paper as saying "We find it curious that the Democrats would attack the governor for giving hard-working, middle-class families a tax break."
